lark_entry.speaker: narrator
lark_entry.text: On the twenty-first morning after receiving the returns watch account, Lin Yue reached Lark Pass behind an ordinary mule cart. Four days of coach road and two nights at paid roadside inns lay behind her. The last climb had been on foot because the innkeeper would not promise wheels on a surface his own animals avoided. The four coach days cost six copper; the two road inn nights cost four, meals included. Her earned fifth stage traveled with her, along with a shoulder whose cleared work stayed below the sudden overhead catches freight people might imagine she could make.

lark_entry_002.speaker: narrator
lark_entry_002.text: The pass market occupied terraces cut into the gorge's eastern wall. A gallery hung beneath the lowest shops, with freight baskets moving along its timber face. Lin heard a bell before she could see the rigger pulling its rope. Each stroke arrived a little late after the movement of his arm. She stopped beside a low wall and watched until the next cart cleared the gallery. Dust settled on a row of dried pears. Nobody looked up to discover whether the newcomer had brought an important destiny.

lark_entry_003.speaker: narrator
lark_entry_003.text: A vendor offered her a cup of hot barley water and asked where she intended to sleep. Lin showed the lodging address written on her ordinary reservation. The woman pointed above the market, then looked at the pack riding on Lin's shoulder. She suggested the longer stepped approach rather than the narrow ladder beside the freight house. Lin thanked her and chose the steps. A useful first answer had cost two copper for the drink, and it had come from someone who knew the current passage rather than her cultivation record.

lark_entry_004.speaker: narrator
lark_entry_004.text: The lodging keeper found her reservation beneath three delivery notices and a child's drawing. Her room was small, with a shutter that had to be lifted before it would close. She tested it with her cleared ordinary grip and left the difficult last inch alone. The keeper brought a wooden prop instead of praising her restraint. Lin liked him for that. She paid four copper for two nights and their meals and asked where letters could be collected. The receiving board stood at the freight association, he said, where nobody should trust a message merely because its paper was expensive.

lark_entry_005.speaker: narrator
lark_entry_005.text: She unpacked her training book, the permitted records she owned, and the last archive receiving account. None of the archive's originals or entrusted keys had come with her. The new freight association had requested applicants explain a completed task, including what their choice had left unfinished. Lin had answered with the returns watch rather than a grand account of advancement. At the market she would need the actual account again. Its two decisions had changed material and service, and a new employer could not fairly assess her by selecting the outcome it preferred.

lark_e01_material_gate.speaker: narrator
lark_e01_material_gate.text: At the receiving window, the association clerk asked which stock had survived the old storm. Lin put the signed receiving beside her application and waited while he read its actual selection. The answer would determine which offered source she could use in the pass's first comparison workshop. An employer could request a new account, but could not manufacture the teaching pages, usable approach or timely delivery missing from the completed watch.

lark_e01_books_001.speaker: narrator
lark_e01_books_001.text: The sixteen annotated lesson booklets had survived because the workers covered the annex breach. Their later custodian's receipt identified the collection without giving Lin ownership of it. Before her departure, the teacher had offered one permitted comparison excerpt from the familiar goat example for this application. Its copy named the source and the teacher's conditions. Lin handed that excerpt over now. The Lark clerk could use a real preserved teaching example, while the ruined short approach and the canceled storm delivery remained plainly recorded beside it.

lark_e01_books_002.speaker: narrator
lark_e01_books_002.text: The clerk asked whether the entire booklet collection could be sent north. Lin said no. She had permission for the one excerpt offered to her, not a traveling library or a license over the teacher's annotations. He removed a larger copying request from his list and placed the authorized example beside the workshop proposal. The small refusal changed what the association could promise its first group. It would have to obtain other materials from its own workers instead of announcing the archive's collection as a free contribution.

lark_e01_books_003.speaker: narrator
lark_e01_books_003.text: The excerpt concerned a goat's route around a gate whose apparent width changed when a loaded basket was counted. Lin had laughed at the example when she first heard it. At Lark, freight baskets hung below a timber edge with nearly the same problem of overlooked width. She wanted to claim the old page had prepared her for this pass. Then she saw the clerk mark its actual scope: a way to ask a comparison question. It qualified no gallery, load or support here.

lark_e01_books_004.speaker: narrator
lark_e01_books_004.text: The first workshop's applicant place offered to her was a lesson-comparison task. Its leader would ask her to distinguish the offered example from the local baskets before any public explanation. That work would take the morning slot otherwise used for a route walk. Lin read the task twice and kept its lost alternative in view. A preserved page had opened an opportunity that the other storm outcomes could not supply. It had also put a familiar error within reach: explaining what she recognized before examining what she had actually arrived to learn.

lark_e01_books_005.speaker: narrator
lark_e01_books_005.text: The clerk retained a permitted reference copy and returned the original offered excerpt to Lin. She checked the receipt's source line before folding it into her bag. The old short approach remained closed until its own replacement treads were supplied; the old courier booking had paid two copper after cancellation. Neither loss disappeared because a Lark teacher liked the surviving example. Lin would have to explain a chosen preservation without using this new invitation as proof that everyone else should have wanted the same choice.

lark_e01_path_001.speaker: narrator
lark_e01_path_001.text: The covered short approach had survived the storm, while the sixteen annotated booklets had become unusable and the courier's departure had been canceled. The local keeper had offered Lin a dated public route note for her application after receiving her request. It described the inspection and its conditions, not a right to use every path called short. Lin gave the permitted note to the Lark clerk. The teacher's three shared school texts still existed elsewhere, but the familiar lost goat pages were not waiting inside her bag.

lark_e01_path_002.speaker: narrator
lark_e01_path_002.text: The clerk looked for the teacher's annotated example because an earlier recruitment circular mentioned it. Lin pointed to the line excluding the soaked booklets from usable stock. He put the circular aside instead of asking her to reconstruct the page from memory. That decision removed one advertised exercise from the association's first comparison workshop. A new example would need an author, permission and actual observations. Her memory could explain why the loss mattered without pretending the original teaching work had traveled intact.

lark_e01_path_003.speaker: narrator
lark_e01_path_003.text: The dated route note recorded a safe approach at the old village under its particular inspected conditions. A rigger reading beside the clerk asked whether she could now inspect Lark's suspended gallery. Lin said she could walk a cleared ordinary route with its keeper and record what she observed. She could not import a favorable result from another valley. The rigger smiled at the word cleared and tapped the part of his own boot where a projecting nail had once gone through.

lark_e01_path_004.speaker: narrator
lark_e01_path_004.text: The first applicant place offered to her was a keeper-led lower-route walk. Its paid leader would retain every judgment about the gallery supports and freight movement. Lin could compare how a route described access with what a person carrying a basket could actually do. The morning lesson-comparison slot went to someone bringing other material. Her old preservation had opened a different useful task here. It also required cold hands, unfamiliar steps and enough patience to avoid answering a structural question from the confidence of a tidy route note.

lark_e01_path_005.speaker: narrator
lark_e01_path_005.text: The clerk copied only the offered public note, wrote its inspection date on the reference cover and returned Lin's own sheet. The old booklets remained lost. The storm courier booking had paid two copper after cancellation. A route that still served ordinary village journeys had value even where the reading annex's later service changed, but that value did not preserve an absent collection or a missed dispatch. Lin carried the new walk invitation upstairs with a clearer sense of what the pass would ask her to notice.

lark_e01_cart_001.speaker: narrator
lark_e01_cart_001.text: The covered cart had delivered its return packets on the original dates. He Xi had earned four copper for the completed delivery, while the sixteen lesson booklets were lost and the short approach remained closed. Before Lin left, the courier had offered a permitted receiving example for her employment application. It showed booking, delivered scope and actual payment without copying household addresses. Lin put that example before the Lark clerk. Its ordinary distinction between accepting work and finishing it seemed likely to matter in a place where freight moved through several hands.

lark_e01_cart_002.speaker: narrator
lark_e01_cart_002.text: The clerk asked whether the old teacher's annotations came with the example. Lin said the collection had become unusable. He asked whether the preserved village approach could support a route lesson. She said it had not been preserved under the cart outcome. He crossed both proposed contributions out. The timely packets were valuable enough to name without borrowing two other results. The revised recruitment cover now described a delivery comparison instead of a library-and-access demonstration nobody could honestly supply.

lark_e01_cart_003.speaker: narrator
lark_e01_cart_003.text: A freight worker glanced at He Xi's receipt and asked why the payment appeared after the receiving line. Lin explained only the actual agreement recorded there: the accepted delivery earned four when its scope was completed. A canceled booking under the other outcomes paid two. The worker said his own canceled baskets sometimes consumed more than two copper of waiting food. Lin agreed the old example could not settle his wage. It could help him identify which terms a new employer needed to state before expecting gratitude.

lark_e01_cart_004.speaker: narrator
lark_e01_cart_004.text: The first applicant place offered to her was a dispatch comparison beside the association's wage reader. She would examine authorized receiving lines and report what they did and did not establish. She would not adjudicate another worker's claim or turn a courier's permission into general access to household packets. The morning route-walk place went to someone else. Her old choice had kept replies moving and now opened a job involving work and payment, with less time for the gallery observations she had hoped to make first.

lark_e01_cart_005.speaker: narrator
lark_e01_cart_005.text: The clerk retained the offered reference copy and returned Lin's own receiving example. He Xi's earned four remained his pay, not a travel subsidy for her. The old short approach still needed replacement treads, and no Lark copying task could restore the ruined lesson annotations. Lin put the new dispatch invitation beside her own wage record. She could describe a completed delivery without claiming it had been worth more than every lost lesson to the people who would have used them.

lark_e01_service_gate.speaker: narrator
lark_e01_service_gate.text: The clerk next checked the later service receiving. Material had been protected before the service decision, and he kept their dates in that order. The present location and hours of the old reading work would determine who could answer the association's reference request. Lin could seek a different future at Lark without turning one inspected reading into a whole surviving term or moving a closed annex back into operation.

lark_e01_closed_001.speaker: narrator
lark_e01_closed_001.text: The old outstation's remaining rainy-term bookings had been canceled. Ten copper had paid its actual stock handling and notices, and two had returned unused. The mountain desk held the receiving role now, beyond the ordinary reach of some former readers. Lin had requested her employment reference there before departure. Its reply arrived with the keeper's accepted scope: a description of her completed duties, not a certificate that nearby public access had remained available.

lark_e01_closed_002.speaker: narrator
lark_e01_closed_002.text: The Lark clerk proposed asking Sun to answer a reference question at the former annex on its next ordinary date. Lin stopped him. There was no operating rainy-term date there under the closure outcome. A question could go through the mountain desk's actual contact or to Sun directly under terms she accepted, but the old canceled room could not supply a convenient audience. He changed the proposed address and warned that the slower mountain reply would miss tomorrow's recruitment discussion.

lark_e01_closed_003.speaker: narrator
lark_e01_closed_003.text: Lin could begin the ordinary application with the reference already received. She could not promise the followup would arrive before the first assignment. The missing nearby service had become an employment uncertainty here, one small part of a larger cost some old readers bore more heavily. She signed permission for the clerk to send the specific public-duty question to its actual receiver. It asked nothing about Sun's private notebook, house or new runoff statement.

lark_e01_closed_004.speaker: narrator
lark_e01_closed_004.text: The association reserved her applicant task provisionally, pending its own direct observation rather than an invented reply from a closed room. The clerk said provisional as though it might offend her. Lin said it was useful to know what he had not established. She left the desk with a place to demonstrate her own current work and one dated unanswered request. The old closure remained a closure, even where the new pass offered her another beginning.

lark_e01_reserved_001.speaker: narrator
lark_e01_reserved_001.text: The old twelve-copper reserve plan had produced one inspected reading in the sound waiting room. Its attendants and carriage had completed their accepted scopes. Later outstation dates had remained canceled without another funded and inspected arrangement. The teacher had given Lin a permitted account of that actual occasion for her reference request. It described the selected material and attendance without calling the limited session a restored public term.

lark_e01_reserved_002.speaker: narrator
lark_e01_reserved_002.text: The Lark clerk asked whether a second reading could receive his followup question next week. Lin showed him the line limiting the plan to its one completed occasion. The question would need the existing actual receiving contact, not a second audience funded by money already spent. He removed a proposed session date from the recruitment cover. The first reading's success remained useful evidence of performed work, and its finite end remained part of the same evidence.

lark_e01_reserved_003.speaker: narrator
lark_e01_reserved_003.text: Lin's reference could describe how the group used the available material, including the teacher's own permitted observations. It could not include private family addresses or assume every former reader had obtained a place. The clerk approved the narrow account for an initial applicant task and left his further question on a separate request slip. He seemed disappointed by how little of the old occasion could be recruited into a continuing advertisement. Lin was beginning to recognize that disappointment as ordinary work.

lark_e01_reserved_004.speaker: narrator
lark_e01_reserved_004.text: The association would observe her new task directly while waiting for any later accepted reply. A preserved occasion had opened a different reference path from a surviving institution. Lin took the dated slip and the provisional assignment rather than promising that the people who attended would gather again on demand. Their next calendars belonged to them. The one reading had mattered because it had actually happened, not because she could carry its audience wherever another employer wanted certainty.

lark_e01_transferred_001.speaker: narrator
lark_e01_transferred_001.text: The old public receiving service had moved to the village school. Twelve copper had paid the accepted transport and three introductory sessions; subsequent access used the school's agreed ordinary hours. The old annex remained closed. Lin had requested her employment reference through the school keeper before traveling, with the permission of the people whose offered observations it included. The new location supplied a current contact instead of an outstation date that no longer existed.

lark_e01_transferred_002.speaker: narrator
lark_e01_transferred_002.text: The Lark clerk found the school's ordinary hours inconvenient for his own recruitment discussion. He asked whether Lin could instruct the keeper to open early. She said the transferred service had accepted its own timetable; she had no appointment or authority to change it. He could send a question for the next ordinary receiving interval or seek another source. The more durable institution was not a room permanently available to her simply because she had proposed its transfer.

lark_e01_transferred_003.speaker: narrator
lark_e01_transferred_003.text: The present school keeper had already answered the specific completed-work question. Its reference named the available teaching stock and excluded storm-soaked pages from usable material. It also mentioned that several former readers disliked the new hours. Lin wanted to explain the practical advantages before the clerk reached that line. She let him read it. A reference worth using could contain another person's dissatisfaction with a choice she had made carefully.

lark_e01_transferred_004.speaker: narrator
lark_e01_transferred_004.text: The association accepted the received reference for its own initial task while reserving judgment about her current practice. Any further source question would follow the school's actual ordinary schedule. Lin signed the narrow permission and took the provisional invitation. A working contact had removed one uncertainty here, while her lack of command over it remained explicit. The transferred service continued with its own people. Her journey had not turned their institution into a department of her ambition.

lark_e01_common_001.speaker: narrator
lark_e01_common_001.text: When the reference work was finished, the clerk wrote three words above her application: Observe before offering. Lin asked whether every applicant received them. He said the association had paid dearly for promises made by people who recognized an old machine in a new valley. She suspected he also enjoyed having a phrase worth repeating. Both things could be true. She put the morning task in her own calendar and asked the simpler questions about its receiving place, hours and possible payment.

lark_e01_common_002.speaker: narrator
lark_e01_common_002.text: The applicant observation was not a work shift. The association would pay its current task leader; Lin could accept one observed try without wages, or decline and leave her application incomplete. She had agreed to that condition in the invitation before booking the road. Any later employment needed separate terms. The clerk gave her the written condition instead of telling her that opportunity should be compensation enough. She read it, accepted the single bounded observation, and kept her longer willingness out of the margin.

lark_e01_common_003.speaker: narrator
lark_e01_common_003.text: A man carrying two broken basket ribs stopped at the desk while she was folding the paper. He wanted a receipt for returning them, although the association clerk had already seen the damage yesterday. The clerk pointed at his informal note. The man pointed at the repair contractor's formal receiving book. Lin watched them reach an irritated agreement about where the ribs would actually be entered. Neither needed her explanation of good records. She moved aside so the man could put down what he had carried.

lark_e01_common_004.speaker: narrator
lark_e01_common_004.text: On the gallery terrace she met Chen Rui beneath a canopy patched with blue cloth. He recognized her after looking at the employment board, then looked as though he would have preferred a less public recognition. His current client was the association's supplier committee. He had arrived three days earlier under a defined contract to compare offered source licenses and terms. That client did not appoint him as Lin's adviser. He stated the conflict before either of them could enjoy turning the meeting into a convenient reunion.

lark_e01_common_005.speaker: narrator
lark_e01_common_005.text: Lin told him she was applying for ordinary work and hoped to find qualified further instruction. Chen said both plans could become expensive if she let them share a purse without naming which service she was buying. Then he noticed the cup in her hand and asked whether the barley water was any good. She said it was hot. He accepted that as enough reason to buy his own. Their old acquaintance had not made the client conflict disappear, but it left them something ordinary to do while the canopy shook.

lark_e01_common_006.speaker: narrator
lark_e01_common_006.text: Chen's contract covered six committee meetings and a written comparison, with payment following the received work. He was not hired to certify equipment, determine structural causes or acquire someone else's private source by the force of a fluent question. Lin asked whether his employer understood those limits. He said the limits were written clearly enough that the committee had begun calling him unhelpful. He smiled with professional satisfaction, then admitted he wished the fee had been higher for work that made people dislike him so early.

lark_e01_common_007.speaker: narrator
lark_e01_common_007.text: The supplier committee wanted a more predictable freight season. Its supporters pointed to baskets reaching the town late, fruit spoiling below the market and repair crews waiting for parts. Workers pointed to temporary posts that became permanent duties without permanent pay. Chen had authority to compare proposed contracts, not to decide whose disappointment mattered most. Lin listened while a basket moved along the suspended gallery below them. The creak that interrupted his sentence seemed too physical to fit neatly inside either group's account.

lark_e01_common_008.speaker: narrator
lark_e01_common_008.text: 'You are listening to the wrong creak,' Chen said. Lin looked at him. He pointed toward the canopy pole beside her, which had been rubbing against the shop beam whenever wind came up the gorge. The freight gallery had made a different sound a moment earlier. She laughed at herself and stopped trying to make the first minute in a new place yield a profound warning. Chen looked pleased for longer than the correction deserved. She let him enjoy the small advantage.

lark_e01_common_009.speaker: narrator
lark_e01_common_009.text: She asked about the bell she had heard on arrival. Chen named the ordinary warning sequence printed on the freight board, then told her to learn it from the actual keeper rather than his retelling. Three short strokes halted new entry to the lower gallery. Two spaced strokes asked the next posted guide to report. A continuous ringing meant the operator had lost the normal sequence and people should use the instructed cleared exit. It sounded less elegant than a magical alarm, and that was why Lin wanted its written limits.

lark_e01_common_010.speaker: narrator
lark_e01_common_010.text: The pass had an old relay at the uphill bell house, but its sound load used association-owned fuel. A novice's rated isolated command could close a control input under supervision; it would not supply the bell's voice or brace timber. Lin kept her current record separate from the relay's job description. Four primary pairs allowed short independently tested tasks, not a new source for the entire gorge. Chen said applicants with brighter robes were often harder to persuade of that distinction.

lark_e01_common_011.speaker: narrator
lark_e01_common_011.text: Lin's robes were dusty enough that she could accept the remark without answering for brighter applicants. She asked which people kept the route and the bench. Chen named the gallery supervisor and Jiang Tao's local survey appointment. Duan Zhi was expected later for a separately agreed instruction term, after completing his own earlier work and travel. Lin had not been accepted as his student. An examiner whose old leg required a supported stance would be unlikely to applaud a newcomer who mistook wanting instruction for already owning his days.

lark_e01_common_012.speaker: narrator
lark_e01_common_012.text: Below the canopy, a freight porter passed with an empty basket and an expression Lin could not read. Chen greeted him by name. The porter asked whether the new comparison would end with another committee paying itself to discover that workers needed shoes. Chen said the commission had no shoe allocation. The porter answered that the absence had never prevented an impressive summary. Lin waited until he had gone before asking whether Chen had included ordinary equipment in his questions. He opened his notebook and showed her a line he had crossed out.

lark_e01_common_013.speaker: narrator
lark_e01_common_013.text: He had removed the line because its proposed source was an unaccepted workers' questionnaire. The committee wanted to quote its answers before anyone had agreed how the questions would be asked or who would receive the result. Lin said a better questionnaire might still be useful. Chen agreed, and told her that useful work was exactly what became easiest to announce without paying for it. He would propose a bounded accepted survey at the next meeting. Whether the committee funded it remained an actual choice ahead.

lark_e01_common_014.speaker: narrator
lark_e01_common_014.text: The afternoon freight movement slowed when a mule refused the lower turn. Its driver stopped pulling and examined the load's left edge. A basket handle had twisted into the neighboring crate's rope. Lin watched an ordinary delay acquire three different explanations in less than a minute. A shopkeeper blamed the driver, a waiting carrier blamed the cramped turn, and a child said the mule disliked dried pears. The driver freed the rope before answering anyone. The mule moved forward and kept its own opinion unrecorded.

lark_e01_common_015.speaker: narrator
lark_e01_common_015.text: Lin descended by the longer public steps to see the gallery from its cleared viewing place. A painted line kept visitors away from the load path. She stayed behind it. The suspended structure had more supports than her first view had suggested, and one section had been replaced with timber of a different color. She could notice the change without identifying its date, strength or workmanship by appearance. An ordinary keeper approached and asked whether she was looking for an entrance. She showed the applicant invitation instead of naming her stage.

lark_e01_common_016.speaker: narrator
lark_e01_common_016.text: The keeper read the invitation and told her the morning task did not grant access tonight. He offered to point out the public exit boards from where they stood. Lin accepted. One board led uphill to the market steps, another across a stone landing to the rigger's shelter. A third was turned inward and marked closed pending its scheduled inspection. She wanted to ask what had happened there. The keeper told her where its public notice could be read and went back to watching the moving freight.

lark_e01_common_017.speaker: narrator
lark_e01_common_017.text: At the notice board, a missing fastener had been recorded as an observation under inspection. The notice did not call it the cause of every delay. The closed passage remained out of use while the keeper awaited a qualified check and repair authority. Lin copied the public inspection date into her notebook. She did not copy private worker names from the neighboring wage sheet. The two notices occupied the same board because space was short, not because structural findings and someone's payment had become the same source.

lark_e01_common_018.speaker: narrator
lark_e01_common_018.text: A child selling boiled chestnuts stood at the bottom of the steps with one adult tending the brazier beside him. He offered Lin a paper cone that was too large for the number she asked to buy. She paid one copper for the smaller portion and watched him fold a new cone badly enough that two chestnuts rolled out. The adult let him recover them with the ordinary scoop and begin again. Lin ate while the second cone took shape. The pass contained teaching that would never receive a cultivation certificate.

lark_e01_common_019.speaker: narrator
lark_e01_common_019.text: She returned to the lodging before her shoulder grew tired. The keeper had fixed the shutter's difficult corner with a plane and moved the prop to another room. He did not ask her to test the repaired movement harder than she could comfortably use it. Lin opened and closed the shutter once, then left it alone. From the window she could see the upper bell house and the first dark folds of the gorge. The market looked smaller from here, while the freight movement continued to sound like several ordinary people doing different work.

lark_e01_common_020.speaker: narrator
lark_e01_common_020.text: Her mother had enclosed a short letter inside the last permitted family packet. Lin read it after washing the road dust from her hands. The letter contained a question about whether the northern grain tasted as disagreeable as an old neighbor claimed, a description of a patched kitchen stool, and an instruction to eat before writing an answer. It did not contain a new diagnosis or a secret explanation for the old lake cost. Lin put it beside the cup and realized she had already postponed supper to admire the view.

lark_e01_common_021.speaker: narrator
lark_e01_common_021.text: The lodging kitchen served millet, greens and a little bean paste within the paid room provision. Lin sat opposite a woman mending a freight glove with ordinary thread. The woman asked whether she was another inspector. Lin said she was an applicant. The distinction interested her more than Lin expected. An inspector could make her husband wait outside a work entrance; an applicant might wait with him. Lin listened to the missing thumb of the glove catch on the needle and asked which place the woman would recommend for buying a replacement.

lark_e01_common_022.speaker: narrator
lark_e01_common_022.text: The woman recommended repairing this pair first. Her husband had worn the leather into a shape that made a new stiff glove awkward at the basket hook. She was not claiming every worn tool should be kept forever. She asked Lin to try the seam without pulling it hard. Lin kept the movement within her comfortable grip. The glove lay against her palm differently from the new training cuffs she remembered. She had been about to answer an equipment question by the price of something not yet fitted to its user.

lark_e01_common_023.speaker: narrator
lark_e01_common_023.text: At the next table two young carriers argued about a contest held at the freight yard. One wanted to enter because a supplier had noticed last season's winner. The other said the winner had spent more on treatment than the offered prize. They disagreed about the dates and stopped short of agreeing that either version was certain. Lin wondered how many conversations the association comparison would have to hear before it could state one accurate sentence. Chen's six meetings began to look less extravagant than they had under the canopy.

lark_e01_common_024.speaker: narrator
lark_e01_common_024.text: After supper she wrote her mother three lines and crossed out the one calling the pass beautiful. It was beautiful, but the word would give the people at home almost nothing she had actually seen. She described the mule's entangled basket rope and the child's chestnut cone instead. Then she admitted the view had made her late for supper. The letter still did not explain every feeling she wanted to share. It was small enough that she might finish and post it before another task made perfection attractive.

lark_e01_common_025.speaker: narrator
lark_e01_common_025.text: She wrote a separate note for the freight application. Her current earned fifth-stage record established four independently tested primary pairs under the kiln method. Its measured reserve had qualified at thirty-six actual usable units and ninety percent compatibility after recovery and sampling. Those historical readings did not state tonight's available charge. Her current application stayed within its brief half-unit input over four ordinary breaths, a quarter-unit useful task, independent stop and complete release. Ordinary eating, sleep and a fresh local assessment would come before any powered observation here.

lark_e01_common_026.speaker: narrator
lark_e01_common_026.text: The shoulder limit received its own line. Comfortable cleared waist work did not certify a sudden overhead catch, a heavy suspended basket or an untested reinforcing grip. Lin could hear how the line might sound to a recruiter who wanted a convenient extra pair of hands. She kept it plain anyway. If it cost an unsuitable job, the loss would be real; pretending the employer would respect her candor enough to hire her regardless would only turn caution into another form of vanity.

lark_e01_common_027.speaker: narrator
lark_e01_common_027.text: At dusk the bell gave two spaced strokes. Lin looked up from her writing and nearly went to the window as though the sequence had summoned her. It summoned the posted guide, whose actual name stood on the duty roll. She was not that guide. She sat down again, listened until the ordinary market noise resumed, and finished the application note. The pass had offered her a first place to observe. It had not offered her the responsibility of every person whose work she could hear.

lark_e01_common_028.speaker: narrator
lark_e01_common_028.text: Before sleeping, she checked the next morning's receiving place, starting bell and task leader against the written invitation. The old storm receiving remained folded with its actual material and service outcomes. Her mother's letter stayed outside the application packet. Her stage record and shoulder limits belonged together. She set her shoes where she would not have to search for them in the dark and loosened the pack strap. Tomorrow she would begin with the particular work a person had actually agreed to watch.

lark_e01_night_001.speaker: narrator
lark_e01_night_001.text: A knock came before she had extinguished the lamp. The lodging keeper brought a message from the freight desk, carried by a porter already returning to this stair. It confirmed the applicant observation and warned that the gallery could close before morning if the scheduled keeper found a new defect. Lin would report to the public receiving point in that case. The porter waited while she read it. He wanted her initials against the delivered notice, then wanted to go upstairs where his supper was cooling.

lark_e01_night_002.speaker: narrator
lark_e01_night_002.text: He introduced himself as Qin Bo when she asked which name the receiving should use. Lin wrote it clearly instead of a title that might fit half the pass. Qin said titles were pleasant until somebody needed to find the person who had been paid. His own job tomorrow began at the basket stores, not the viewing gallery. If he appeared beside her task, he would be passing through on another accepted duty. Lin noticed how quickly a familiar face could become an imagined available helper.

lark_e01_night_003.speaker: narrator
lark_e01_night_003.text: Qin had left two basket ribs at the freight desk earlier. His repair contractor had now received them, and the unresolved part concerned the date of the replacement. He did not ask Lin to make the dispute disappear. He asked whether she had seen the clerk enter the return. She had seen arrival and the clerk's agreement, not ink entering the book. He looked relieved, thanked her, and said he would request her statement only if the receiving book failed to show the actual entry.

lark_e01_night_004.speaker: narrator
lark_e01_night_004.text: After he left, Lin added the delivered notice to the application packet and kept the possible worker statement separate. She had arrived to seek a livelihood and qualified further instruction. Already a person had asked for a small piece of evidence she could actually supply. She wanted to feel useful without becoming hungry for every such request. Qin's cooling supper was a good limit to remember. He had another evening beyond the broken ribs, and she had no reason to keep him standing while she admired her own caution.

lark_e01_night_005.speaker: narrator
lark_e01_night_005.text: Below the lodging, the last market shutters closed in an uneven sequence. A child counted their sounds until an adult asked him to count bowls instead. Lin heard the argument turn into laughter and then into a dispute about who would carry the wash water. She laid the mother's letter flat under the cup so the paper would not curl. Home and Lark remained different places with different work; affection could join them without making either one available whenever the other required a convenient answer.

lark_e01_night_006.speaker: narrator
lark_e01_night_006.text: The market bell fell silent while freight lamps stayed lit below. Lin imagined the people still working beneath them and stopped herself from inventing their opinions of the newcomer. Some might welcome an observer; some might have tired of observations whose makers left before paying for changes. Tomorrow they could tell her themselves. She closed the shutter with the repaired ordinary movement, set the training book beyond the spilled-water edge of the table, and turned the lamp down until its flame no longer distracted her.

lark_e01_night_007.speaker: narrator
lark_e01_night_007.text: Sleep came slowly, without a useful dream or hidden instruction. Her shoulder felt tired from the road rather than transformed by ambition. She moved the folded blanket beneath her arm and found a comfortable ordinary position. The pass kept its timber, fuel, workers and unanswered questions outside the small room. Lin would meet them in daylight with a paid lodging receipt and one accepted observation interval, which was a modest beginning large enough to require her actual presence. The keeper had shown her an ordinary stair exit before taking payment.

lark_opening_contract_001.speaker: narrator
lark_opening_contract_001.text: The receiving account had reached her before this journey, closing the old two appointments rather than offering new wages for either. On the following morning, the mountain archive keeper offered a different finite job. Twelve two hour sorting shifts would run from the third through fourteenth days after that receipt. The work concerned ordinary current index slips at the mountain desk, not the damaged outstation or another judgment of household rights. Lin accepted the new scope before the keeper assigned its first tray. Her shoulder could manage seated light papers within its existing limits.

lark_opening_contract_002.speaker: narrator
lark_opening_contract_002.text: The archive had accepted thirty six new service copper for those twelve shifts, three payable after each completed receiving. A separate thirty two paid its lodging provider for sixteen actual days of room and meals, beginning with the offer and ending before her coach departure. Both sources came from the current mountain desk appropriation, not the earlier review or storm grant. The provider confirmed the offered place before she accepted. That finite living provision left the sorting wages available for the road. No promised future Lark wage had financed her arrival.

lark_opening_contract_003.speaker: narrator
lark_opening_contract_003.text: On the third morning she found two slips for the same household filed under different hills. One offered a public delivery date; the other named a private repair visitor. The keeper asked for the public index corrected without copying the visitor's particulars into it. Lin had to ask which sheet supplied the date before deciding the two slips could be joined. Her first three copper came after that completed two hours. A familiar household name had made the mistake tempting, and a modest paid task had made stopping possible.

lark_opening_contract_004.speaker: narrator
lark_opening_contract_004.text: By the seventh shift she knew the tray whose folded corners caught beneath the drawer. She proposed flattening every slip, then stopped when a reader explained that his raised corner let an ordinary stiff finger separate one page from another. The keeper kept that reader's folder apart and asked Lin to count only the loose current index leaves. She changed the method without treating the reader as an obstruction. The job did not require another channel opened in her body. It required her to learn which convenient improvement would take somebody else's grip away.

lark_opening_contract_005.speaker: narrator
lark_opening_contract_005.text: The twelfth shift ended on the fourteenth day. Its receiver counted the completed trays and paid the last three copper, bringing the actually received sorting wages to thirty six. Lin retained that sum for the new journey without counting the earlier six copper appointment or four copper returns shift as unspent savings. Those older payments remained completed facts, not an amount this new purse needed to borrow. She gave the keeper her intended Lark receiving address for the permitted reference. The drawer with the raised corners stayed with its actual readers.

lark_opening_contract_006.speaker: narrator
lark_opening_contract_006.text: Two rest days followed within the provider's sixteen day living scope. Lin washed her road shirt without the sudden wringing her shoulder still disliked, packed only papers she owned or could carry under permission, and received the final meal before departure. The coach began on the seventeenth morning. Its fare and the two road inn nights reduced the new thirty six to twenty six before the pass. She had not arrived rich. She had arrived with a paid route behind her and enough current money to hear an employment offer without needing it already accepted.
